plan.title: Young Minds: Science, Reading and Creativity Day

tasks.label: Approve programme, invitation, venue and expenditure
Organise science demonstrations and check materials
Coordinate seating, printed materials, refreshments and supplier quotations
Select pupil presentations, supervise rehearsals and prepare project labels
Supervise demonstrations, display areas and pupil movement
Supervise collection of pupils, clean venue, return equipment, reconcile spending and record feedback

drafts.invitation:
Young Minds: Science, Reading and Creativity Day
Confirmed Date: Saturday, 21 November 2026
Venue: Multipurpose Hall

Dear Parents and Guardians,

Sunrise Learning Centre, Abuja, warmly invites you to our first “Young Minds: Science, Reading and Creativity Day.”

This special educational event is designed to showcase the wonderful progress our pupils have made in the classroom. During the programme, you will have the opportunity to see live science demonstrations, enjoy storytelling and reading presentations, and explore creative project displays prepared by the children. Our goal is to celebrate their learning and provide inspiration for practical educational activities at home.

Attendance for this event is free.

Registration: 09:30
Programme Start: 10:00
Venue: Multipurpose Hall
Organizer: Sunrise Learning Centre, Abuja

Warm regards,

Mrs Grace Okoro
Headteacher
On behalf of Sunrise Learning Centre

---

Programme Schedule:
09:30 Registration
10:00 Welcome and housekeeping (10 minutes)
10:10 Opening remarks by the headteacher (10 minutes)
10:20 Pupils’ reading and storytelling presentations (15 minutes)
10:35 Science demonstrations (35 minutes)
11:10 Refreshment break (15 minutes)
11:25 Guided viewing of pupils’ project displays (30 minutes)
11:55 Parent and pupil reading activity (20 minutes)
12:15 Creativity presentations and recognition of participants (25 minutes)
12:40 Vote of thanks (10 minutes)
12:50 Closing remarks and supervised departure (10 minutes)

Safety and Supervision:
- Science activities must use simple, low-risk classroom materials. Avoid flames, exposed electrical connections, sharp tools, or experiments involving hazardous chemicals.
- Teachers must supervise all demonstrations, display areas, and pupil movement.
- Parents should remain with younger children during the guided display tour.
- Mr Samuel Eze (First-aid officer) will be available throughout the programme.
